The image appears to be genuine. But according to The Niagara Falls Illumination Board, the falls was lit up in teal (a blue-green color) on Tuesday for an Alzheimer's Awareness Month event, not blue to celebrate the Democratic Party's wins in the 2026 midterm elections.
As major U.S. news outlets reported that the Democratic Party had gained a majority in the U.S. House and Senate in the 2026 midterm elections on Tuesday, an image (archived) circulated online that social media users claimed authentically showed Niagara Falls in Canada lit up in blue in celebration of the result.
One Threads user shared the image of Horseshoe Falls, part of Niagara Falls in Canada, lit up in blue and wrote, "Canada lights up Niagara Falls in blue, sending a powerful message of solidarity with the Democrats and their blue tsunami unfolding. 💙🌊🇨🇦"
The image also circulated on Facebook, Instagram and X (archived, archived, archived). Snopes readers contacted us about the claim.
Though the image appears to be genuine, the claim that Niagara Falls was lit up in blue to celebrate Democrats' midterm wins is false. The Niagara Falls Illumination Board, a six-member U.S. and Canadian organization, decides what color to illuminate the falls every night, and there was no evidence it decided to celebrate the Democrats' midterm wins on Tuesday.
Rather, according to the board's schedule, it lit up the falls in teal on Tuesday for Alzheimer's Awareness Month. According to the Alzheimer's Foundation of America, the illumination board participated in its "Light the World in Teal" event that was part of the awareness month.
Sandy Silverstein, a spokesperson for the Alzheimer's Foundation of America, wrote that Niagara Falls participated in the awareness event on Tuesday, the day after 1,783 other landmarks reportedly did so. Silverstein wrote in an email to Snopes on Wednesday:
Niagara Falls has been part of this initiative for a number of years and asked if they could light up November 3 this year because of a scheduling conflict. We are grateful for their continued efforts to raise Alzheimer's awareness and show support for the families affected by it through participating in this program.
We contacted The Niagara Falls Illumination Board through Niagara Parks to confirm its online schedule was correct. We also contacted a Threads user who claimed to have taken the photograph of the blue light on Niagara Falls to ask when they did so. We await replies to our queries.
Snopes has not independently verified the source of the image that some social media users said showed Niagara Falls lit up in blue on Tuesday night.
The online artificial intelligence detectors Pangram, OpenAI's Verify tool and Google's Gemini SynthID scan found no traces of AI in the image, suggesting it was authentic — meaning not created with AI or digitally edited. The image displayed no obvious signs of AI generation.
Assuming the image was indeed authentic, the difference between the planned teal lights and the blue lights seen in the image could be a product of the colors' natural proximity to each other or the lighting settings used on the camera that captured the image.
It was also possible the photo showing the blue lights was taken on a different date. The Threads user who claimed to have taken the photo wrote:
I'm very happy for the USA and their election results but it's wild to me how many people just stole the photo I took of the Falls, reposted it, and made up their own story and assumptions about when it was taken. I was showing my support for the blue wave, as others have done with sharing their "blue" photos, but I never stated when my photo was taken.

How does this fluoride-free toothpaste compare when it comes to oral health?
How you brush your teeth — and what you use to do it — matters.
Recently, dentist Dr. Jin-Ho Phark says he's noticed patients asking about fluoride-free toothpaste options. Phark is an associate professor of clinical dentistry at the Herman Ostrow School of Dentistry of University of Southern California.
"There's a lot of interest from the patients," Phark says. "I hear that also regularly from students."
One product that patients are asking about in particular is a calcium phosphate mineral called hydroxyapatite. Many patients, Phark says, may have seen the products on social media, "being pushed by influencers and other people quite intensively."
The traditional fluoride toothpaste became common in the late 1950s, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, when Procter & Gamble Co. released Crest nationally. Over the next few decades, oral care products with fluoride as their active ingredient became widely available around the world. These products help protect the outer layer of teeth from cavity-causing bacteria.
And dental health is important because it's related to so many systems in your body, from your heart to digestion.
Want the latest stories on the science of healthy living? Subscribe to NPR's Health newsletter.
"There are these connections made between your oral health, and the bugs that you have in your mouth, and systemic health and even the composition of your gut microbiome," says Dr. Livia Tenuta, a dentist who specializes in preventing tooth decay and associate professor at the University of Michigan School of Dentistry.
The claim
The promise of hydroxyapatite? Many of the things you care about when it comes to toothpaste: cavity protection, whitening, enamel-strengthening. But without fluoride.
Health experts widely agree that fluoride — a naturally occurring mineral — is beneficial to health. But curiosity is growing about fluoride-free options.
"There is an increasing number of people who are refusing fluoride totally, or hesitant to take it, especially for their children," says Bennett Amaechi, a professor of dentistry at the University of Texas at San Antonio.
That hesitancy stems from a history of skepticism about fluoride. Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has blamed the fluoridation of water for a number of health problems, including arthritis, bone fractures, bone cancer, IQ loss, neurodevelopmental disorders and thyroid disease.
Low levels of fluoride are generally considered safe and key to preventing cavities. Amaechi says there's no concrete evidence about potential harms of fluoride when it comes to children's IQ. And research that has found associations between fluoride and IQ has looked at very high levels of fluoride — over twice what's recommended in the U.S. water supply. The CDC previously named the addition of fluoride to public drinking water one of the top 10 great public health achievements of the 20th century, alongside vaccinations and family planning. They also say fluoride in water reduces cavities by 25%.
Still, Kennedy's criticism of fluoride seems to have made its way to toothpaste — and opened up space for products that use hydroxyapatite instead.
So what is hydroxyapatite?
The hype around hydroxyapatite is, in part, due to its similarity to tooth enamel. There's also some research that suggests hydroxyapatite can help with tooth sensitivity.
Tooth enamel is mostly made of calcium and phosphate. Those minerals form the outer layer of your teeth, which protects the internal layers of tissues, nerves and blood vessels, from damage.
Your enamel is stronger than your bones, but still susceptible to damage over time from things like sugary foods and dental plaque. Bacteria in your mouth feed on sugars, and produce acids that eat away at the outer layer of your teeth. Tenuta says over time, that process sets the stage for tooth decay, often referred to as caries, or eventually cavities (a hole in a tooth that comes from this decay).
She says fluoride toothpaste helps protect teeth by "remineralizing" them with calcium and phosphate.
"When [fluoride is] available in our saliva, in the dental plaque that we were not very perfect in brushing, that fluoride that is left over after brushing with the fluoride toothpaste will actually bring minerals back to the tooth," Tenuta says.
Fluoride works with those minerals to form a new compound that protects teeth. It acts like a shield for your enamel. But you need to brush with fluoride toothpaste consistently. Dentists recommend twice daily to keep those minerals around in our mouths.
Hydroxyapatite is thought to work in a slightly different way. These products seem to get into tiny crevices in the tooth enamel.
Many hydroxyapatite products use a form called nano-hydroxyapatite, which has smaller particles that, in theory, can more easily penetrate pores in enamel, though research data is limited.
The evidence
Amaechi, who studies hydroxyapatite use, says fluoride is extensively researched, especially in long-term studies. But he says early research on hydroxyapatite is positive.
"When it comes to remineralization and preventing caries manifestation, it is as effective as fluoride," Amaechi says.
Amaechi was an author on a 2021 study in the journal Scientific Reports, that followed 177 children for almost one year, and compared hydroxyapatite toothpaste to fluoride toothpaste. The researchers tracked tooth decay in each group, and found that both groups had similar outcomes. That study included funding from Dr. Wolff Group, a German company that owns two brands that make hydroxyapatite toothpastes.
That company contributed funding to another study, published two years later in the journal Frontiers in Public Health. Researchers found similar results after tracking 171 adults, comparing tooth decay in participants using a hydroxyapatite toothpaste to those using a fluoride toothpaste for 18 months. Both groups showed similar outcomes, suggesting that hydroxyapatite worked as well as fluoride in the study. However, the participants in the study were mostly healthy young adults without any severe oral health problems.
Tenuta says she'd want to see more long-term studies, especially in people with high risk of tooth decay.
"There are very few studies and they recruited participants of low caries risk," she says.
One shorter-term study in 2019, published in the Journal of Investigative and Clinical Dentistry, did compare a hydroxyapatite toothpaste to fluoride toothpaste in 133 people who were at higher risk of caries. After a little over five months, the researchers found both toothpastes performed similarly.
The bottom line
Hydroxyapatite toothpastes tend to be more expensive than fluoride ones — some over a dollar more expensive per ounce.
For patients who are open to both options, "I will advise them to use fluoride because fluoride has more evidence supporting its efficacy," Amaechi says.
Tenuta agrees.
"I would recommend as a best option to stick to a fluoride toothpaste because that's what we have a lot of evidence behind," she says.
The American Dental Association, a professional group for dentists, said in an email to NPR they acknowledge more people are using products with forms of hydroxyapatite and that some evidence suggests those products can contribute to remineralization.
However, research on the ingredient is new, "and evidence regarding its clinical effectiveness remains limited and ambiguous, especially regarding clinical indications," wrote ADA Consumer Advisor spokesperson Dr. Ada Cooper.
Instead, the ADA recommends you brush your teeth twice a day for two minutes with a fluoride toothpaste, floss daily and regularly visit a dentist.

The Directorate of Enforcement (ED) has conducted search and seizure operations at five premises linked to persons and entities allegedly involved in a counterfeit medicines racket in Karnataka. The agency has also frozen a bank account containing approximately ₹9 lakh belonging to one of the accused.
The searches were conducted under Section 17 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002, as part of an ongoing money-laundering investigation arising from an FIR registered at Tavarekere police station on August 18, 2026.
The case originated from a joint raid conducted by the Drug Controlling Authority and police personnel at a residential property in C.K. Tandya village on August 18. During the raid, the accused were allegedly found storing medicines and pharmaceutical drugs without valid licences, permits or authorisations and replacing labels on the stored medicines. A Special Investigation Team (SIT) led by Vamsi Krishna, Joint Commissioner (West), Bengaluru is probing the case.
The FIR was registered under Section 318(4) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, and Section 63 of the Copyright Act, 1957. Since these offences are scheduled offences under the PMLA, the ED registered an Enforcement Case Information Report (ECIR) and initiated a money-laundering investigation.
According to the ED investigation, a man identified as R. Prashanth allegedly arranged a farmhouse near Bidadi to manufacture, repackage and relabel medicines without the requisite drug licence or permit.
Cheap bulk pharmaceutical formulations allegedly sourced from manufacturing centres in various States were repackaged into new vials and fraudulently labelled as expensive Pfizer antibiotics, including Zavicefta and Emblaveo. Although the vials allegedly contained generic medicines, they carried labels bearing the Pfizer brand name.
The counterfeit medicines were allegedly distributed through M/s DM Pharmaceuticals and supplied to M/s Krupa Healthcare. The latter subsequently supplied the medicines to other pharmaceutical entities and hospitals, mixing them with genuine medicines to avoid detection, the ED said.
During the searches, the agency froze bank accounts belonging to Veeresh Kumar containing approximately ₹9 lakh. Digital devices, records and other incriminating documents belonging to various persons were also seized.
Further investigation is underway to identify the extent of the alleged money-laundering network and trace the proceeds of crime.

Joshua Wong, face of Hong Kong's pro-democracy protests, jailed for 10 years
- Published
Joshua Wong, once the face of Hong Kong's democracy movement, has been sentenced to 10 years in jail for colluding with foreign forces under the city's sweeping national security law.
Wong, 30, is among hundreds of campaigners and ordinary Hongkongers arrested under the law, which was imposed in 2020 following explosive pro-democracy protests against Beijing's growing control.
Critics say the far-reaching law has silenced dissent, but authorities argue that it is needed to maintain stability and deny it has weakened the city's cherished autonomy.
Wong, who has been in custody for the last six years, has already been imprisoned multiple times for his activism which started when he was a teen.
- Silenced and erased, Hong Kong's decade of protest is now a defiant memory 
  - Published30 November 2024
- What a defiant mogul's trial says about Hong Kong 
  - Published18 December 2023
On Thursday, Wong arrived in court wearing a dark blue long-sleeved shirt, khaki trousers and black-rimmed glasses. He looked slimmer compared to his previous public appearances.
He nodded in greeting towards members of the packed public gallery, and took notes intermittently as the judge read out the reasons for his sentencing.
A crowd had gathered outside the court, with dozens of Hongkongers having queued for hours hoping to get a seat in the public gallery. There was also a heavy police presence.
Wong is already serving time for subversion and was due to be freed early next year when he was handed the latest charges, which he has pleaded guilty to earlier in September.
Two months and two days of the 10-year term will be served concurrently with his ongoing sentence, the judge said on Thursday.
Prosecutors said that Wong had conspired with other campaigners, including self-exiled activist Nathan Law, to lobby for foreign sanctions and blockades against Beijing.
These activities took place between July and late November 2020, the court heard.
Wong and Law had been co-founders of Demosisto, a now defunct pro-democracy political party.
The charges against Wong "underscores the authorities' fear of prominent dissidents and shows the lengths they will go to keep them behind bars for as long as possible", rights group Amnesty International had earlier said.
Who is Joshua Wong?
Born to IT professional Roger and homemaker Grace in October 1996, Wong was diagnosed with dyslexia as a child, which made him struggle with school.
However, he was quick to challenge established rules and norms when they didn't make sense. In secondary school, he rallied with his classmates to protest against the high prices of canteen lunches on Facebook.
In 2011, Wong, then 14, co-founded the pro-democracy student activist group Scholarism, which quickly grew in size and influence.
The following year, the group rallied more than 100,000 people to protest against Hong Kong's plans to implement mandatory "patriotic education" in schools, forcing the authorities to back down.
Wong, who was just eight months old when Hong Kong was returned from British to Chinese control, has devoted much of his life thus far towards addressing the strictures Beijing has imposed on his home city.
By 2014, Wong, who was then at the forefront of a civil disobedience movement known as the "Umbrella Movement", had already become one of the most recognisable faces of Hong Kong's pro-democracy movement.
In 2016, he co-founded Demosisto with Law and Agnes Chow, an activist who is now also in exile.
But he often expressed discomfort at being labelled a "protest leader".
"We have a lot of facilitators in this movement and I'm one of them... Instead of having a top-down command, we now have a bottom-up command hub," Wong told The Financial Times in November 2019.
Demosisto disbanded in 2020, the year Beijing introduced the controversial National Security Law (NSL) in Hong Kong.
Law left for the UK and continued his advocacy abroad, while Wong stayed on in Hong Kong and tried to run for a seat in its legislature – but was barred, with authorities citing his opposition to the NSL as one of the reasons.
Meanwhile, the court cases against Wong were stacking up.
On 23 November 2020, he pleaded guilty to several charges related to his involvement in protests outside the Hong Kong police headquarters in 2019.
Then came the NSL charges. While still in prison in February 2021, Wong was among 47 people charged with "conspiracy to commit subversion". The group became known as the Hong Kong 47 and remains the largest prosecution so far under the NSL.
Wong was still serving his 56-month sentence for the subversion conviction when he was charged with collusion under the NSL last year.
On 22 November 2020, the day before he pleaded guilty to the protest charges, Wong wrote in a post on Instagram addressed to "the people of Hong Kong": "To be honest, I have never had much faith in Hong Kong's politics, but I have every confidence in the people of Hong Kong.
"Even as political power now poses a comprehensive challenge to the resilience of our civil society, I believe the people of Hong Kong will, as always, find a way to see things through."
The harshest NSL sentence thus far had been handed to former media tycoon Jimmy Lai, who was jailed for 20 years, also for colluding with foreign forces.

As India and the US work to finalise a long-awaited trade deal, the ruling Republicans' major electoral loss in the recently concluded US midterm polls has raised crucial questions: How may this flip in the US Congress affect the India-US negotiations? Will the setback to US President Donald Trump's party give India room to negotiate? Experts believe that the Republican Party's stinging loss in the midterm elections, which shifted the balance of power in the US Congress, may push Trump to accelerate negotiations that had been reportedly stalled over tariff concerns. This, however, may not make the "US trade policy less restrictive," they said. Another expert explained why India may get some room to negotiate on “substance rather than under deadline pressure.” Professor Rituparna Kaushik, Assistant Professor at FLAME University, told Mint that the midterm election results will not rewrite US trade policy overnight. This is because "the Section 301 and Section 232 duties [under which tariffs were imposed] rest on executive authority and any rollback faces a presidential veto," he said. He believed that a Democratic Congress with oversight powers "makes abrupt tariff escalation politically harder, which gives India room to negotiate on substance rather than under deadline pressure." "Labour-intensive exporters in textiles, apparel, and gems and jewellery stand to gain most from that stability," he said. On India’s strategy, Kaushik said New Delhi must "secure a predictable, rules-based tariff schedule rather than chase short-term concessions, and to broaden engagement beyond the White House to Congress and US states." "At the same time, India must keep diversifying through the EU agreement and other partners, so the US remains a key market but not a single point of vulnerability. On agriculture and dairy, India should hold firm, as US farm-lobby pressure cuts across party lines," he added. Ajay Srivastava, Founder of the Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI), said on Friday that "bad" midterm election results could push Trump to focus more on trade negotiations and fast-track the proposed agreement with India. "I think the bad election results for Mr Trump will nudge him to expedite trade relations with India, and he may be expediting that trade agreement. It may happen sooner than we think," he told ANI. According to Srivastava, with Trump facing domestic political constraints, he may seek an early trade agreement with India to demonstrate his influence on the international front. "With Trump weakened in the domestic field, he will have only trade to concentrate and I think he will push for an early India-US trade deal," he said. While Trump's domestic political setback may accelerate efforts to conclude an India-US trade agreement, the Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI) expects Washington's broader protectionist trade approach to remain largely unchanged. The GTRI, in its latest report, cautioned that the midterm setback would not necessarily make US trade policy less restrictive. Srivastava indicated that the threat of additional US tariffs linked to India's purchases of Russian crude oil could remain a negotiating tool for Washington. He told ANI that the US could use this threat to encourage India to sign the proposed trade agreement, potentially imposing additional tariffs of around 17–19 per cent rather than the much higher level previously discussed. Srivastava claimed that senior officials and ministers from both countries had been engaged in discussions and that negotiations were close to completion, although some differences remained. He said the proposed Graham Act had earlier led to expectations that the US administration would take around 60 days to decide on the matter. With some of that period already elapsed, he expects the trade agreement to be concluded within approximately two months. India and the US had agreed to a framework for the deal in February, which brought down to 18 per cent from 50 per cent the punitive tariff on most Indian goods imposed in August last year. In the meantime, the US Supreme Court invalidated Trump's use of emergency powers to impose sweeping tariffs globally, leading to a 10 percent baseline rate. But a final deal between two of the world's biggest economies remains elusive. In recent months, the India-US talks have faced complications, most recently a new US law that paves the way for up to 100 percent tariffs on Indian goods due to New Delhi's purchase of Russian oil. A deal has also been held back because Washington is yet to complete a Section 301 trade investigation on several nations over alleged excess industrial capacity, Reuters reported on October 6. The probe is to evaluate whether such overproduction is hurting or undercutting American industries. Unless this probe is completed, it is hard to tell what final tariff Indian goods will attract, the report added. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said earlier in September that negotiations had reached a broad understanding, but the continuing Section 301 process remained an important factor in deciding when to finalise the agreement. What do India and the US want? India has sought to keep dairy, poultry, rice, wheat and other farm products outside the scope of market-opening commitments. It wants greater certainty over US tariffs before making concessions. The Trump administration wants India to cut Russian oil purchases, arguing Indian purchases of Russian crude help finance the war in Ukraine. What's at stake: The US is India's largest export market. Analysts told Reuters earlier that in the absence of a trade deal, India risks higher US tariffs from the ongoing trade probe and purchase of Russian oil, even if it could negotiate for waivers under the sanctions law. Another increase in tariffs could hurt businesses, dent market sentiment and hurt the Indian currency, which is already trading close to record lows. For 2025, India's total goods exports to the US reached $103.82 billion, while US exports to India totalled approximately $45.6 billion, for a total bilateral trade of $149.42 billion, according to ANI. The bilateral services trade in 2025 was recorded at $92.23 billion, where India exported $48.67 billion worth of services to the US and imported $43.56 billion worth of services from the US. Democrats have officially won full control of both chambers of the US Congress in the November 3, midterm elections. This historic shift ends the Republican Party's unified control in Washington, delivering a major political setback to President Donald Trump midway through his term. Democrats last won a majority in the Senate in 2022, before Republicans went on to win control of the chamber in 2024. The victory will have implications for control of Washington, as Trump enters his final two years in office. With the majority, Democrats can block the president's nominees and control what measures receive votes on the floor, severely limiting his ability to get anything done legislatively. Rwanda's army team removed from Africa league after US sanctions, NBA says
- Published
The National Basketball Association (NBA) says it removed Rwanda's army team from its African league because of US sanctions imposed on the country in March.
The NBA had previously said the Rwandan army-funded Armée Patriotique Rwandaise (APR) club would not participate in the 2026 Basketball Africa League (BAL).
However this is the first time the NBA has revealed the reasons behind the APR's removal.
The association was responding to complaints by two US senators, who sent a letter asking them to reconsider their partnership with the Rwandan team. The US placed sanctions on the Rwandan army, accusing it of fuelling the conflict in the Democratic Republic of Congo in March.
The senators said the NBA risked "becoming complicit in sportswashing by accepting money from a Rwandan government that systematically abuses human rights".
Last week, the US also imposed sanctions on Rwanda's defence ministry over its support for the M23 rebel group which has seized control of large parts of eastern DR Congo. Rwanda denies backing the rebels despite overwhelming evidence.
Rwanda is an official BAL partner and pays the league to host its finals at the 10,000-seat BK Arena in the capital, Kigali.
The BBC has asked Rwanda for comment.
- What is the Basketball Africa League? 
  - Published14 May 2021
- The evidence that shows Rwanda is backing rebels in DR Congo 
  - Published29 January 2025
In the letter to the NBA dated 23 October, Democratic Senator Jeffrey Merkley and Republican counterpart Marsha Blackburn gave the association until 2 November to give a written response regarding its continued partnership with Rwanda.
"What is the NBA red line for accepting money from foreign governments that commit human rights abuses?" the senators asked.
Among other queries, they also questioned how the association could "reconcile its continued partnership with Rwanda with its purported commitment to justice".
In its response, NBA deputy commissioner Mark Tatum said the Rwandan team "had been withdrawn" from the BAL following the sanctions imposed earlier in the year, American sports website ESPN reports.
The NBA said the APR basketball club would remain barred while the US sanctions are in place.
The APR is one of Rwanda's top basketball teams and represented the country in the BAL in 2024 and 2025, when it came third. It was replaced by the RSSB Tigers this year.
The BAL is a pan-African basketball league established and co-organised by the NBA and the basketball's world governing body Fiba.
It is a professional league featuring 12 club teams from across the continent.
Rwanda has hosted all but one of the league's final and playoff matches since the inaugural match in 2021.
The NBA reportedly receives millions of dollars annually from the country for the marketing and partnership rights.
DR Congo has repeatedly condemned Rwanda's high-profile international sports deals, including with the NBA, European football clubs and Formula 1, asking them to end their campaigns.
It argues that these help Rwanda clean up its global image, while the conflict continues in eastern DR Congo.

Health intel-sharing group warns industry in wake of cyberattack on French blood bank
In a new security bulletin, the information sharing and analysis center devoted to the healthcare industry, Health ISAC, alerted members to a recent wave of cyberattacks targeting refrigeration controllers — including one incident that affected a major French blood bank.
"This alert is issued for situational awareness, highlighting how recent operational technology (OT) attacks against specific refrigeration brands directly intersect with emerging threats to the health sector," reads the bulletin seen by NPR. Operational technology refers to the machines that control physical processes in the real world, from cooling systems to water pumps.
Cyberattacks on grocery stores and food processing plants everywhere from Europe and Israel to U.S. military bases have drawn headlines in recent months, particularly as attacks have resulted in spoiled food, fires, broken machinery, and major business disruptions. Attackers are clearly aware of the vulnerability of these systems and are taking advantage.
However, until news broke that the French blood bank, known as the French Blood Establishment, had also been targeted, there was less public attention focused on the potential consequences of refrigeration controllers failing in other industries, particularly healthcare, where lifesaving implements like blood and vaccines often require finely tuned temperature-controlled environments to remain viable.
"This incident underscores a stark operational reality: cybersecurity in healthcare is fundamentally about patient safety," wrote Errol Weiss, the chief security officer at Health ISAC in an email to NPR. "When threat actors manipulate operational technology like cold-chain storage and refrigeration units holding donor blood, plasma, or critical therapies, they aren't merely stealing data or locking down administrative files, they are directly endangering the physical resources required to sustain human life."
On Thursday, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, the FBI, the Department of Health and Human Services, and the U.S. Department of Agriculture published their own fact sheet about threats to industrial refrigeration and cold chain monitoring systems, tools they identify as critical to multiple industries from healthcare to chemical production, food and agriculture, and transportation.
The FBI Cyber Branch Operations director, Brett Leatherman, said the bureau is tracking bad actors targeting these systems "across critical infrastructure sectors globally, putting inventory and equipment at risk."
"Industrial refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems protect food, medicine, and other temperature-sensitive products, making them attractive targets for malicious cyber actors," Leatherman said.
Iran, Russia and the search for the culprits
The French blood bank confirmed in a press release Tuesday that one of its vendors used in cold storage rooms was targeted by malicious cyber activity, resulting in the defrost and temperature thresholds being raised dangerously high. The French Blood Establishment ultimately managed to detect the suspicious activity in time to rescue blood samples.
It remains unclear who is responsible for the global attacks on refrigeration controllers, and whether it's multiple actors or groups.
Iran has been linked to at least one incident in Israel earlier in the spring, though that breach involved a lot more sophistication and malicious activity. Investigators probing the disruptions at U.S. military bases are also considering Iran as the potential culprit.
Meanwhile, two pro-Russian hacking groups, NoName057(16) and Z-Pentest Alliance, belatedly released videos and posted on Telegram claiming responsibility for the attacks across Europe, publishing a sample of alleged hacked credentials that would've allowed them to access equipment including machines made by the Danish company Danfoss and the American company Copeland. Those machines can monitor and control temperature and other functions. The hacking groups have some history of targeting refrigeration controllers and other operational technology. However, it's unclear if the recent wave of attacks on refrigerators and freezers across Europe even required stolen credentials to execute, a factor that has led some cybersecurity experts to be skeptical of their claims.
Even so, it will require more evidence like access logs, configuration changes, and connections between maintenance accounts on the controllers to make any clear assessments, explained Tom Hegel, who leads threat intelligence research at cybersecurity firm SentinelOne.
"Russian-aligned actors are a credible hypothesis because there is a credible precedent, including the refrigeration-related attack DOJ attributed to CyberArmyofRussia_Reborn and NoName's history of politically motivated disruption. But that is only the context, not the missing evidentiary link to these European incidents," Hegel told NPR.
"It's important to note that such Russian threat actors often seek attention and claim to cause incidents even when false," he continued.
Regardless of who's responsible, the incident highlights how these nearly ubiquitous tools used to remotely manage critical systems are vulnerable to attack in several different ways.
For one, thousands of the refrigeration controllers in France alone were exposed to the open internet with almost no protection put in place before unidentified hackers went after them in October. Afterward, experts were still tracking hundreds of devices left unprotected. That's just a fraction of the tens of thousands of exposed operational devices online, many of them embedded in critical infrastructure.
Additionally, many of the major remote management systems used in refrigerators and freezers have security vulnerabilities. After alerting the companies to the problems, cybersecurity firm Claroty published research on vulnerabilities in multiple major refrigeration controllers, including those made by both the American manufacturer Copeland and by Danfoss.
While some of those vulnerabilities have been discovered and the vendors have designed patches to seal the hole, the problems don't stop there.
Experts warn it's difficult to patch operational technology because doing so often requires shutting systems down. In industries like healthcare, even minutes of downtime create extreme risk for patient safety. And for some aging models, it's impossible to patch, because the vendor is no longer offering updates — and companies can't afford to spring for a new model.
Sometimes, executives don't even know what machines are on their networks.
Additionally, for many companies, vendors that work with them demand remote access to systems like refrigeration controllers to regularly service them. It's often a requirement in the contract companies sign.
"Industrial chillers operate under vendor contracts that mandate persistent remote access," explained Nic Adams, CEO of 0rcus, a U.S. offensive security firm. "These commercial agreements leave national food and medical supplies defenseless against basic credential abuse."
Finally, hackers are now using AI to find these vulnerabilities faster than ever, and AI is also helping them to better understand the complex machines and the processes they control. Bad actors a world away no longer need to understand individual languages or industries, or even the physics involved to disrupt operations. In recent weeks, cyber incident responders tell NPR they're seeing a massive spike in attacks that are at least in part carried out by AI agents.
The good news is that a lot of these attacks, even if they incorporate AI, are not particularly sophisticated, novel, or stealthy.
Weiss of Health ISAC tells NPR there are basic steps the healthcare industry can take to prevent being a victim of these opportunistic attacks.
That process "begins" by "eliminating public internet exposure," wrote Weiss, then "enforcing strict network segmentation" in order to isolate refrigeration systems "from standard enterprise and guest networks" and finally adding on safeguards "that software overrides cannot bypass" like "hard-wired mechanical cutoffs" and "independent thermal alarms."
In the Health ISAC alert, the industry is urged to separate not just refrigeration controllers from hospital IT systems, but also medical gas monitors, for one, and train staff onsite on how to take physical manual control of machines in an emergency.
Finally, the alert urges hospitals to have offline backups of their systems.
Store managers on the frontlines
Sharing intelligence about these kinds of cyberattacks can help other potential victims avoid disaster.
While Estonian grocery stores were targeted in the most recent wave of attacks, many of those store managers were on high alert thanks to warnings issued by Estonia's Information Systems Authority, RIA. "When one Selver store was attacked on 2 November, the attackers managed to change the refrigeration system's temperature setting to +50°C. However, the service provider reacted quickly and prevented significant damage," said Annika Müür, a spokesperson for RIA. "So while we can't say that Estonia managed to prevent the attacks entirely, I think this case is a good example of the importance of monitoring threats internationally, acting on early warnings and working closely with businesses to minimise the impact."
Weiss of Health ISAC also urged companies across sectors that are being targeted by this recent wave of attacks to share information to help others defend themselves.
"The attack highlights why timely, trusted information sharing across borders and sectors is our strongest collective defense," he wrote.
"Rapid intelligence sharing allows hospitals and health facilities globally to recognize emerging attack patterns, verify vendor exposure, and harden critical infrastructure before threat actors can cause physical harm."

Women recruited from economically weaker sections were being offered ₹20,000 to ₹30,000 for an egg donation cycle, while those operating the alleged racket made an average of about ₹3 lakh from each cycle.
Malkajgiri police widened their investigation into the exploitation of women, falsification of records and the role of IVF and fertility establishments.
The 43 women rescued during simultaneous raids in Hyderabad have undergone medical examinations, including blood-group and fitness tests. Police are now verifying their medical histories with IVF centres to establish their treatment records.
The investigation has raised concerns over how the women were recruited and whether they gave informed consent for the procedures. Police said women from economically weaker sections were targeted and that, in some cases, intermediaries allegedly even completed their signatures on documents. Investigators are examining possible falsification of records and whether the women fully understood the procedures they were being recruited for.
Police are tracing the payments and commissions involving organisers, recruiters and intermediaries who connected the women with fertility-related establishments.
The investigation is now expanding to medical establishments. Police are preparing to serve notices to the District Medical and Health Officer (DMHO) and conduct searches at ART and fertility centres. Some hospitals have also approached police and informed them that employees found to have been involved had been removed.
Investigators are examining how women from West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and other states were recruited, transported and accommodated in Hyderabad before being referred for egg retrieval procedures. Their medical records, consent documents and the procedures they underwent are also being scrutinised.
All eight accused arrested in connection with the Hyderabad cases have been remanded to judicial custody. Further investigation is underway.

రోడ్డుపై నడుచుకుంటూ వెళ్తున్న ఓ బాలికను కొందరు వ్యక్తులు కిడ్నాప్ చేసిన ఒక వీడియోను బీహార్లో జరిగిన సంఘటన అంటూ సోషల్ మీడియాలో షేర్ చేస్తున్నారు (ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ). ఈ వీడియోలో నంబర్ ప్లేట్ను కప్పి ఉంచిన బొలెరో వాహనంలో వచ్చిన కొందరు వ్యక్తులు బాలికను బలవంతంగా ఎత్తుకెళ్లడం కనిపిస్తుంది. వారి నుంచి తప్పించుకోవడానికి బాలిక ప్రయత్నిస్తుండగా, అటుగా వెళ్తున్న ఓ బైకర్ ఈ ఘటనను వీడియో తీస్తూ, కిడ్నాపర్లను అడ్డుకునేందుకు ప్రయత్నిస్తాడు. దీని వెనుక ఎంత నిజముందో ఈ కథనం ద్వారా తెలుసుకుందాం.
క్లెయిమ్: బీహార్లో రోడ్డుపై నడుచుకుంటూ వెళ్తున్న ఓ బాలికను కారులో వచ్చిన కొందరు వ్యక్తులు కిడ్నాప్ చేసిన నిజమైన ఘటనను ఈ వీడియో చూపిస్తోంది.
ఫ్యాక్ట్: ఇది ఒక స్క్రిప్టెడ్ వీడియో. ఇది బీహార్లో నిజంగా జరిగిన కిడ్నాప్ ఘటన కాదు. Isa Stuntతో కలిసి వీడియోలు చేసే ముక్లేసుర్ అలీ (Muklesur Ali) ఈ ఘటన ముందుగా ప్లాన్ చేసి చిత్రీకరించిందని, వీడియోలో కనిపించిన వారందరూ తన టీమ్ సభ్యులేనని తెలిపారు. అంతేకాకుండా, వారితో సంబంధం ఉన్న ఇన్స్టాగ్రామ్, యూట్యూబ్ ఖాతాల్లో కూడా వినోదం కోసం ఇలాంటి అనేక స్క్రిప్టెడ్ వీడియోలు ఉన్నట్లు గుర్తించాం. కాబట్టి, ఈ పోస్టులో చేసిన వాదన తప్పు.
వైరల్ వీడియోలోని కీ ఫ్రేమ్లను ఉపయోగించి రివర్స్ ఇమేజ్ సెర్చ్ చేయగా, 2026 అక్టోబర్ 11న ‘Isa Stunt’ అనే ఇన్స్టాగ్రామ్ ఖాతాలో ఇదే వీడియోను (ఇక్కడ) పోస్ట్ చేసినట్లు గుర్తించాం (ఆర్కైవ్). అయితే, వైరల్ వీడియోలో ఉన్నట్లుగా ఈ వీడియోలో ఆడియో లేదు. దానికి బదులుగా బ్యాక్గ్రౌండ్ మ్యూజిక్ ఉంది. అంతేకాకుండా, ఈ పోస్టుకు జత చేసిన క్యాప్షన్లో కూడా ఘటనకు సంబంధించి ఎలాంటి వివరాలు లేవు.
ఆ ఇన్స్టాగ్రామ్ పేజీని పరిశీలించగా, వైరల్ వీడియోను పోలి ఉన్న మరికొన్ని వీడియోలు కనిపించాయి. ఈ వీడియోల్లో (ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ) వైరల్ వీడియోలో కనిపించిన అదే బొలెరో వాహనం, మోటార్ సైకిల్, వ్యక్తి ఉన్నట్లు గుర్తించాం. దీన్ని బట్టి, ఈ వీడియోలు నిజమైన ఘటనలకు సంబంధించినవి కాకుండా ముందుగా ప్లాన్ చేసి చిత్రీకరించినవై ఉండవచ్చని తెలుస్తోంది.
తదుపరి, ‘Isa Stunt’ అనే ఇన్స్టాగ్రామ్ ఖాతా బయోలో ఇచ్చిన యూట్యూబ్ ఛానెల్ను కూడా గుర్తించాం. ఈ ఛానెల్లో వైరల్ వీడియోను పోలి ఉన్న మరికొన్ని వీడియోలు ఉన్నాయి. వాటిలో బాలిక కిడ్నాప్, రోడ్డుపై దాడి, రోడ్డు ప్రమాదం వంటి ఘటనలను చిత్రీకరించారు. అయితే, ఈ వీడియోల వివరణలు ఇంకా ఛానెల్ బయోలో ఈ కంటెంట్ను కేవలం వినోదం కోసం రూపొందించినట్లు పేర్కొన్నారు.
అయితే, ‘Isa Stunt’ ఇన్స్టాగ్రామ్ ఖాతాలో పోస్ట్ చేసిన పలు వీడియోల్లో (ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ) ‘Muklesur Ali’ అనే ఇన్స్టాగ్రామ్ ఖాతాను (ఇక్కడ) ట్యాగ్ చేసినట్లు గుర్తించాం. ముక్లేసుర్ అలీ ఖాతాను పరిశీలించగా, వైరల్ వీడియోను పోలి ఉన్న మరికొన్ని వీడియోలు కనిపించాయి. వీటిలో ఇదే తరహాలో కిడ్నాప్ చేసినట్లు చిత్రీకరించిన ఒక వీడియో కూడా ఉంది. గతంలో కూడా ముక్లేసుర్ అలీ రూపొందించిన పలు వీడియోలు సోషల్ మీడియాలో వైరల్ కాగా, వాటిని నిజమైన ఘటనలుగా తప్పుగా ప్రచారం చేయడాన్ని మేము (ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ) ఫ్యాక్ట్-చెక్ చేశాం. ఈ వివరాలన్నీ పరిశీలిస్తే, వైరల్ వీడియో నిజమైన కిడ్నాప్ ఘటనను చూపించేది కాదని, వినోదం కోసం ముందుగా స్క్రిప్ట్ ప్రకారం చిత్రీకరించిన వీడియో అని తెలుస్తోంది.
NewsChecker ముక్లేసుర్ అలీని సంప్రదించగా, తాను, Isa కలిసి ఒక టీమ్గా స్క్రిప్టెడ్ వీడియోలు రూపొందిస్తామని తెలిపారు. వైరల్ అవుతున్న బాలిక కిడ్నాప్ వీడియో కూడా ముందుగా స్క్రిప్ట్ ప్రకారం చిత్రీకరించిందేనని, అందులో కనిపించిన వారందరూ తన టీమ్ సభ్యులేనని ఆయన స్పష్టం చేశారు.
చివరిగా, బీహార్లో రోడ్డుపై ఓ బాలికను కిడ్నాప్ చేస్తున్నట్లు వైరల్ అవుతున్న ఈ వీడియో స్క్రిప్టెడ్, నిజమైన సంఘటన కాదు.

Banihal, Nov 06: Taking cognizance of concerns raised through All India Radio Srinagar’s current affairs programme Shaharbeen over the alleged prescription of expensive branded medicines by doctors in government hospitals, the Chief Medical Officer (CMO) Ramban has ordered the constitution of dedicated Prescription Audit Committees in all health institutions across the Ramban district.
In a circular issued on November 6, the incharge CMO Ramban Dr Opinder Singh directed Medical Superintendent, District Hospital Ramban, and all Block Medical Officers (BMOs) to constitute committees to examine the allegations and conduct a comprehensive and impartial audit of OPD and IPD prescriptions issued by doctors.
The circular notes that despite the availability of free medicines and generic alternatives in government hospitals, allegations have surfaced regarding certain doctors prescribing expensive branded medicines from outside pharmacies, thereby imposing an unnecessary financial burden on poor patients.
CMO Ramban orders prescription audit across government health institutions.
They will also seek feedback from patients and attendants to ascertain whether they were advised or compelled to purchase medicines or undergo diagnostic tests from particular private shops.
The CMO has further directed the Medical Superintendent and all BMOs to submit comprehensive institution-wise audit reports, along with verified documentary evidence, stock position and recommendations for necessary action, within seven days.
The circular has also been forwarded to the Director Health Services Jammu and Deputy Commissioner Ramban for information.
The directive marks a significant administrative response to the concerns highlighted by Shaharbeen, bringing the issue of prescribing practices and the financial burden on patients in government healthcare institutions under official scrutiny.

The Telangana government has expanded cancer treatment services to all 33 districts in the State, with day-care cancer centres providing chemotherapy locally to reduce the need for patients to travel to Hyderabad, Minister for Health C. Damodar Raja Narasimha said on Tuesday, November 3. The government has also initiated steps to establish Regional Cancer Centres to further strengthen cancer care infrastructure, he added.
The Minister made these remarks during a review meeting on medical services being provided to cancer patients in government hospitals.
Oncologist Dr. Nori Dattatreyudu, who also serves as the advisor to the Telangana government on preventive, curative and affordable cancer care, said 35,000 cancer cases have been registered on the dedicated cancer portal. “Declaring cancer a notifiable disease and effective use of cancer registry will help strengthen the State’s efforts in monitoring and controlling the disease,” he added.
Citing the Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination programme as an example, Dr. Nori also appreciated the State’s efforts in prevention, screening and early detection of cancer. Of the 3.4 lakh eligible girls in Telangana, 2.3 lakh of them have been vaccinated against the HPV, achieving a coverage of 67%, he said.
During the meeting, officials briefed the Minister on cancer treatment facilities available at the MNJ Cancer Hospital and the Nizam’s Institute of Medical Sciences (NIMS), besides the functioning of day-care chemotherapy centres established across the State. They explained that while patients initially receive treatment at MNJ or NIMS, chemotherapy services are subsequently provided at district-level centres. Patients are also being mapped district-wise to facilitate treatment and follow-up.
The Minister directed officials to improve facilities for patients receiving chemotherapy at district centres and ensure that the services were readily available at the district headquarters. “Patients should not have to travel to Hyderabad for chemotherapy when treatment could be provided closer to their homes,” he added.

Measles strategy works – Now it must expand to more countries
Cape Town Measles Declaration pledges to cut measles deaths by half
At a landmark World Health Organization (WHO)/United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) meeting in Cape Town, leading players in the fight against measles spelled out what it will take to stop 2000 children dying every day from this preventable disease. Together with UNICEF special ambassador Angelique Kidjo, they issued a call for intensified efforts and the resources necessary to ensure all children are protected against measles.
“We can do it – we’ve done it before – in Afghanistan, Angola, in countries devastated by conflict and drought and every other form of disaster,” said Carol Bellamy, Executive Director, UNICEF. “In just three years, and against great odds, we’ve cut the number of children dying from measles by almost 25%. It’s one of the most dramatic declines in disease mortality in history. But the next 25% will be harder. With the political and financial support of donors and governments around the world, we can together save many more lives.”
The “Cape Town Measles Declaration” calls on governments to take strong action against one of the world’s most vicious and prolific vaccine-preventable childhood killers – a disease which kills 745,000 children every year. We must control this disease to meet the Millennium Development targets of a 67% reduction in under-five mortality by 2015. The world leaders are well aware of the urgency. Last year, the UN General Assembly Special Session on Children set a 2005 target date to reduce measles deaths from 1999 levels by 50%. This year, the World Health Assembly, which includes 192 member states, endorsed the WHO and UNICEF measles strategy to combat the disease.
“When 30 million children are affected and 745,000 children die every year, you have to think big,” said Dr. LEE Jong-wook, Director-General of WHO. “Since the launch of the WHO-UNICEF strategy to reduce measles deaths in 2000, we have delivered measles vaccine to more than 200 million children globally. We know the strategy works. An additional half a million children are alive today because of all the partners’ efforts. But if we’re to prevent more deaths, we must do more. And we’ll need help from governments and from the international community.”
The campaign against measles has been dramatic – hundreds of thousands of children saved, the virus almost banished from the Americas and transmission cut drastically in many African countries, where the Measles Initiative Partnership has been the driving force behind the campaign. WHO and UNICEF have identified 45 countries as the highest priority for mortality-reduction strategies, accounting for 95% of global deaths from measles.
“It has been astonishing to see the results of the immunization programme in Africa,“ said Dr Mark Grabowsky, Senior Technical Officer, American Red Cross. “Now we have proof that we can reduce measles mortality even in countries torn apart by conflict, if governments are committed, communities are engaged and we have the support of donors, NGOs and volunteers. What we have accomplished so far through the Measles Initiative Partnership gives great hope for the future, and the many thousands of children we can still save.” The foundation of the measles mortality-reduction strategy is the re-invigoration of national immunization systems. At the Cape Town meeting, delegates discussed strategies with governments and policy makers for strengthening routine immunization services and making the life-saving measles vaccine available to all children as a matter of course.
”It’s not just about reducing childhood deaths today. We need to be in this for the long haul and this means a sustainable reduction in childhood deaths, which only a strong national health system can guarantee,” said Dr Stephen L. Cochi, Deputy Director, National Immunization Program, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). ”This kind of international focus and commitment gives us the opportunity to build that strength – boosting safe routine immunization services, establishing international laboratory networks and increasing surveillance to detect and respond to outbreaks.”
“Today the call to action is clear,” said Mr Nick Farrell, Senior Programme Officer, International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. “ We have to ensure every child receives a second opportunity for measles immunization in these 45 countries, no matter how remote or marginalized, regardless of barriers of conflict, culture and poverty.
“To date we have seen tens of thousands of health workers and volunteers trek across mountains and deserts in all kinds of conditions to find these children to ensure they receive the life-saving vaccine,” said Timothy E. Wirth, President of the United Nations Foundation. “We are witnessing incredible commitment from ordinary people. They need – they deserve to be backed up by the world’s political will and financial support.”
Ms Angelique Kidjo, Special UNICEF ambassador, believes that the Cape Town Measles Declaration indicates a clear path towards a giant achievement in children’s health.
”The world has committed, to drastically reducing the devastating, pointless waste of young life,” she said. “If we reach our targets for measles, we will have taken a huge step towards keeping that promise. I believe we can get there – but only if we make it a priority to turn this declaration into action. This goal deserves all we can give. We must do whatever is necessary.”
Further information:
- Of all the vaccine-preventable diseases, measles remains the leading childhood killer. Measles is an important cause of overall under 5 childhood mortality.
- Measles affects over 30 million children. More than 745,000 die each year from measles – more than half of them in Africa.
- A safe, effective and inexpensive measles vaccine has been available for over 40 years.
- Measles accounts for an estimated 50% of vaccine-preventable deaths among children.
- One million measles deaths are already being prevented each year with existing immunization efforts. With the successful implementation of the WHO-UNICEF measles strategy (including routine immunization and periodic supplementary immunization activities), an additional 500,000 measles deaths can be prevented each year.
- Measles is a highly contagious vaccine-preventable disease caused by the measles virus. It is one of the most readily transmitted communicable diseases and probably the best known and most deadly of all childhood illnesses. Measles causes a high fever, rash, cough and can kill. It affects mostly children, but also young adults. Children usually do not die directly of measles, but from its complications such as pneumonia and diarrhea which attack their weakened immune systems.
- It costs less than a dollar to immunize a child against measles.
- A critical goal is to reduce measles mortality by 50% by 2005 (compared to 875,000 deaths in 1999).
- The WHO-UNICEF strategy to reduce measles deaths includes: achieving and maintaining high routine measles immunization coverage – ‘the first opportunity’ to infants; Providing a ‘second opportunity’ for measles immunization for all children through periodic supplementary immunization campaigns; Ensuring high quality measles surveillance is in place to detect and respond to outbreaks; and improving management of complicated cases.
- Collaborating partners include: WHO, UNICEF, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, the United Nations Foundation, humanitarian and non-governmental organizations, including the American Red Cross and the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies, governments of countries affected by measles, development banks, donor governments (e.g. Canada, Japan, the United Kingdom and the United States of America).
- The importance of developing long term immunization planning cannot be underestimated. This includes ensuring measles activities are fully integrated with other national health goals, establishing high quality surveillance, mobilizing necessary human and financial resources and planning for financial sustainability of measles mortality reduction activities.

Quick Answer
Concat is a free, open-source CapCut alternative with offline AI captions, voice cloning, background removal, 100+ effects, and 4K exports. It runs locally, needs no account, and adds no watermarks. Available across major platforms, it’s promising but still in beta, with some rough edges.
When you think of video editing, CapCut is a popular name that would pop up. It has made short-form editing painless. However, it has now started to put more of its tools behind a paywall, and a few of them need an internet connection to work.
If you are looking for a way out, you have probably already seen OpenReel, the browser-based open-source editor, or gone through our list of the best free video editing software. This time we have something different. Concat takes a different route. It is a free, open-source editor that runs on your own computer and is loaded with features like captions, voiceovers, and background removal built in.
Table of Contents
What is Concat?
Concat is a video editor that is currently in beta. The idea behind its development is easy to understand: It wants to give people stuff that CapCut offers but for free, like auto-captions, text-to-speech, background removal, keyframes, effects, titles, and 4K export. Everything Concat has on offer comes without strings attached. You don’t need to sign up, no watermark stamped on your exports, and no premium tier waiting around the corner.
The other big difference is where the work happens. Concat does everything locally, on your machine. It is built on a native Rust engine with a GPU compositor, and the AI models it uses (for captions, voices, and cutouts) are downloaded once from the settings and then run offline. This means the raw footage that you upload never gets uploaded anywhere.
CapCut is still a great editor, and nobody is pretending otherwise. When we compared it with Instagram Edits, we pointed out that CapCut has the richer feature set, but also that some of its tools need a connection and that its template and music ecosystem is tied closely to TikTok, which owns it. And if you are in India, you already know CapCut is banned here. So, you have to download the modded version or depend on some ad-filled alternatives.
That is the gap Concat is trying to fill. Not a “lite” version of a big editor, but a free one that keeps the stuff you reach for every day and keeps it on your own PC.
Concat features that matter
The feature list is long. But here are the parts that stand out.
Auto-captions that work offline
Captions are quite important nowadays, as content is reaching every part of the globe. But it is a chore every Reels and Shorts editor knows too well. Concat handles them using Whisper, a speech-recognition model that runs locally. You pick a model size (you can choose larger models, which are more accurate but require a stronger machine), and styled captions appear straight on your timeline. No upload, no waiting on a server, and it keeps working without internet.
Text-to-speech and voice cloning
Concat gives you free voices for narration, which is handy for tutorials or faceless channels. You can also clone a voice from just a few seconds of recording. That’s nice to edit a flubbed line without re-recording a whole take.
Background removal
You might have removed people or objects from your images. For videos, most of the editors ask you to pay. But Concat lets you edit out people or objects from a clip for free. If the automatic cutout misses a spot, you can paint the mask manually.
Keyframes with a curve editor
With keyframes, you can animate almost anything over time: position, scale, rotation, opacity, volume, and the settings of effects. There is a built-in curve editor too. You can use this to make a zoom feel smooth instead of mechanical, something that a paid video editor offers.
100 effects, filters and transitions
Concat comes with about 100 effects, filters, and transitions. They are rendered by your GPU and show up live in the preview. This way you can see what you are doing instead of waiting for an export to find out.
Fast cutting and a proper timeline
You get everything like split, trim, ripple delete, merge, freeze frame, and speed changes. If you like clips snapping together without gaps, you can switch on a magnetic timeline. Additionally, you can stack as many tracks as you want for overlays and picture-in-picture, keep several timelines inside a single project, and use blend modes like screen, add, and multiply. Crop and flip tools are there as well.
Titles with real styling
You can change fonts, add strokes and shadows, and drop in a background plate behind the words. If you don’t have any ideas, you can start from the already available presets.
One-switch audio cleanup
If your video has bad audio because of a faulty microphone or nearby noise, it can spoil a good video more than bad lighting does. Concat has a simple toggle for noise reduction, voice enhancement, and loudness leveling. You can also change voice effects to chipmunk, robot, and telephone.
Export and performance
Now, the best part is that with Concat, there is no limitation on export. It supports H.264, HEVC, and AV1, up to 4K at 60 frames per second with 10-bit colour.
Which platforms does Concat support?
Concat is versatile and supports multiple operating systems:
- Windows
- macOS
- Linux
- Android
- iPhone and iPad
Moreover, the editor is available in 26 languages. Downloading and setting up Concat is simple. Here’s what you need to do:
- Open the official download page, which picks the right build for your device. You can also grab any version from the GitHub Releases page.
- Install it like any other app on your device.
- On Windows, your system may warn you because the builds are not code-signed yet. Click More info, then Run anyway.
- On macOS, if the system refuses to open the app, the project suggests running xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Concat.app in Terminal.
- Open Settings and download the AI models you want (captions, voices, cutout). After that, they work offline.
Concat vs CapCut
| Feature | Concat | CapCut | 
|---|---|---|
| Price | Free, no subscription | Freemium | 
| Who is behind it | Open-source project (AGPL-3.0) | ByteDance | 
| Internet needed | Only to download AI models once | Some tools need a connection | 
| Templates and music | Limited | Large library tied to TikTok | 
A few things to keep in mind
Concat is promising and has all the features you would need from a video editor that is trying to be an alternative to CapCut. But don’t forget that it is young, and there are a few caveats that you should know about.
- It is a beta. The repo had over 200 open issues at the time of writing this article. So, you may come across some rough edges. We would advise you not to trust it with a client deadline until you have tested it on your own projects.
- Unsigned Windows builds and the macOS quarantine step can feel sketchy to newcomers. But it is safe, even though they are expected for now.
- You do not get a stock library to lean on. You will need your own assets.
- iPhone users have extra work because you have to sideload it, and sideloading is not for everyone.
Once you have the clarity, you should give Concat a try and let its output help you decide if you should keep using it or not. Let us know in the comments below which editor you are currently using.

Saudi Arabia has extended its $3 billion financial support to Pakistan for a longer period, offering Islamabad relief as it grapples with external debt repayments and pressure on its foreign exchange reserves. The rollover also underscores the growing closeness between the two countries, whose relationship has recently expanded beyond financial assistance to defence and regional security cooperation. Pakistan Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb confirmed the extension on Wednesday, saying Riyadh had agreed to keep the financing in place for a “reasonable period”, without specifying a new maturity date. “It has been extended and for a reasonable period. You don't need to worry as to for how long given the kind of strategic relationship we have,” Aurangzeb told reporters in Islamabad, Dawn reported. The $3 billion facility was provided by Saudi Arabia in April to help Pakistan meet a $3.5 billion repayment to the United Arab Emirates (UAE). The financing matured on October 31 under its original three-month term. The extension comes as prospects of a proposed $10 billion US backstop facility for Pakistan appear to have weakened, as per the report. Riyadh had also extended a separate $5 billion deposit for Pakistan until 2028, Dawn reported. Pakistan has been struggling to meet its external financing requirements, including debt repayments and the need to maintain adequate foreign exchange reserves. The immediate pressure behind the latest Saudi financing dates back to April, when the UAE sought repayment of $3.5 billion it had provided to Pakistan. Islamabad repaid the amount, creating a financing gap and putting additional pressure on its foreign exchange reserves. Saudi Arabia stepped in with the $3 billion facility to help Pakistan manage the repayment and shore up its external account. The latest rollover means Islamabad can continue to count on that funding instead of having to arrange an immediate repayment, providing some relief to its strained external finances. Pakistan's dependence on external financial support has been a recurring feature of its economic challenges. The country has also relied on assistance from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to stabilise its economy and manage its balance of payments. According to Aurangzeb, Pakistan is targeting a $4 billion reduction in external debt during the current fiscal year, followed by another $3.5 billion next year. The finance minister has said the government wants to replace expensive short-term borrowing with longer-term financing through bonds and private placements to reduce refinancing risks. Saudi Arabia's financial support is rooted in its longstanding strategic relationship with Pakistan. The two countries have maintained close political, economic and defence ties, with Riyadh repeatedly stepping in when Islamabad faces pressure on its external accounts. The latest extension also follows Saudi Arabia's decision to keep its separate $5 billion deposit with Pakistan in place until 2028. Together, the arrangements provide Islamabad with an important source of financial support as it attempts to reduce its dependence on short-term borrowing. Pakistan has longstanding defence links with Saudi Arabia and remains an important military partner in the region. It is also the world's only Muslim-majority nuclear-armed country. The financial relationship comes amid deepening defence cooperation between Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey. The three countries signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement on August 7, 2026. The agreement seeks to strengthen collective deterrence and stipulates that an armed attack against any one of the three countries would be regarded as an attack against all three. Dawn reported that Pakistan and Saudi Arabia had already completed their ratification processes. The agreement provides a framework for closer defence cooperation and collective security. Pakistan is attempting to manage its debt burden by reducing its reliance on short-term financing and accessing international capital markets. Aurangzeb has said the government is exploring longer-term borrowing options, including Eurobonds, Panda bonds and Pakistani rupee-linked dollar-settled bonds. Pakistan's liquid foreign exchange reserves stand at around $26.86 billion, including $21.47 billion held by the State Bank of Pakistan and approximately $5.41 billion with commercial banks, according to figures cited by the finance minister. There are optimistic plans for spaceflight, and then there are optimistic plans.
AST SpaceMobile is a Texas-based, publicly traded company building very large satellites to provide direct-to-cell communications on Earth. But it has been having trouble finding rides to space. So on Friday, AST announced that it is developing a medium-lift rocket, named Blacklift, which will have the capacity to lift 20 metric tons to low-Earth orbit. Oh, and the company said it would start launching commercially in late 2028.
“The Blacklift rocket is the springboard to significantly expand our total addressable market, providing AST SpaceMobile with regular unconstrained access to orbit and providing for most favorable owner’s economics in the industry,” said Abel Avellan, founder, chairman, and CEO of AST SpaceMobile, in a news release.
To anyone with even a basic understanding of rockets, that timeline is wildly, fantastically, and stupidly optimistic. Still, the announcement is worth examining because it underscores two important trends in today’s launch industry.
First, it’s becoming increasingly apparent that satellite operators planning to deploy large constellations need to secure launch capacity years in advance, as Amazon did nearly half a decade ago. And if they can’t secure that capacity on favorable terms, they are now considering taking the extraordinary step of developing their own rockets.
And secondly, since investors are now recognizing the worsening launch crisis that Ars has been writing about for months, there is apparently capital to be raised for new entrants into the medium-lift launch market. AST is not the only company making fantastical claims of late. A firm called Cowboy Space said in October it was building a large rocket named Big Iron (full credit—that’s an excellent name) to launch orbital data centers. It also claimed its large rocket would make its first flight in 2028.

Travel-focused SaaS company RateGain reported a 46.5% increase in its consolidated net profit to ₹74.7 Cr in the September quarter (Q2 FY27) from ₹51 Cr a year ago. Operating revenue jumped 152.6% YoY to ₹745.4 Cr, reflecting the consolidation of travel marketing platform Sojern, which RateGain acquired for $250 Mn in November last year. Sequentially, net profit declined 21.3% from ₹94.9 Cr, while operating revenue fell 5% from ₹785 Cr. RateGain reported negative other income of ₹26.2 Lakh, taking its total income to ₹745.1 Cr. Total expenses rose about 158% YoY to ₹647.7 Cr. Adjusted for deferred deal consideration related to the Sojern acquisition, RateGain said its net profit rose 78% YoY to ₹90.8 Cr, while adjusted EBITDA more than tripled to ₹169.1 Cr. For H1 FY27, operating revenue increased 169.5% YoY to ₹1,530.4 Cr from ₹568 Cr. Reported EBITDA rose 214.2% to ₹324.5 Cr, while adjusted EBITDA increased 250.9% to ₹362.5 Cr. The company said its reported H1 EBITDA had already exceeded its full-year FY26 EBITDA. Sojern Integration And Debt The Sojern acquisition expanded RateGain’s travel marketing business, particularly its presence among destination marketing organisations (DMOs), hotels, and other travel businesses. To finance the acquisition, RateGain’s UK subsidiary secured a $125 Mn debt facility from HSBC and Citibank, backed by a corporate guarantee from the Indian parent. Including a repayment of $46.3 Mn today, the subsidiary has repaid $93.8 Mn, or 75%, of the original facility. Its outstanding debt now stands at $31.3 Mn. Alongside the expansion in revenue, RateGain said the Sojern integration helped broaden its customer base. It had 14,538 customers at the end of September, about 4.5X the 3,224 customers it had at the end of FY25. Its customers include hospitality companies, online travel agencies (OTAs), airlines, car rental companies, and DMOs. Marketing Drives Business Mix RateGain operates across three verticals: data as a service (DaaS), distribution, and marketing technology. Its offerings span competitive pricing and demand intelligence, hotel distribution, digital marketing, and guest engagement. Marketing technology now accounts for 80.2% of revenue, followed by DaaS at 13.2% and distribution at 6.6%. By customer industry, hospitality contributed 48.6% of H1 revenue, followed by DMOs at 30.9%, OTAs at 7.2%, airlines at 3.7%, and car rentals at 2.3%. North America accounted for 63.7% of H1 revenue, followed by Europe at 21.5%, Asia-Pacific at 12.3%, and other markets at 2.5%. The company’s client roster includes 33 of the world’s top 40 hotel chains, four of the top five airlines, and seven of the top 10 car rental companies. RateGain also highlighted its AI products. Chairman and MD Bhanu Chopra said shifting travel demand is increasing customers’ reliance on data and AI. He said RateGain’s priorities included adding customers, increasing their use of its platform, and extending AI into more of their daily operations. In H2 FY27, the company plans to take the combined RateGain and Sojern offering to more customers. RateGain reported a total pipeline of ₹660 Cr and new contract wins worth ₹277.7 Cr. The company’s employee headcount stood at 1,244 at the end of September, up 42.8% YoY. Shares of RateGain ended today’s trading session 3.3% higher at ₹819.50 apiece on the BSE.

Will Atiku Abubakar be on Nigeria's presidential ballot after court ruling?
- Published
Nigeria's Federal High Court has sacked the leadership of the opposition African Democratic Congress (ADC) party - and also ruled that the nomination of its presidential candidate, former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, is invalid.
A statement from the ADC said the ruling was another desperate attempt to cripple the opposition.
Presidential elections are scheduled to take place on 16 January when President Bola Tinubu's main challengers are again expected to be Abubakar and former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi.
What is the row about?
Several high-profile politicians joined the ADC in 2025 - disillusioned by the factional infighting in the once powerful Peoples Democratic Party (PDP).
Among them were Abubakar - who had served as vice-president between 1999 and 2007 when the PDP was in power - and former Senate president David Mark.
As accommodations were made for the line-up of political heavyweights, Mark took over as its interim chairman.
But Nafiu Bala Gombe, a former ADC national deputy chairman, argued before the court that this was not lawful as Mark and others had not been elected at a national convention.
Instead, he said, he himself should have taken over the party's leadership following the resignation of the ADC's former chairman in 2025.
This is not first time the Federal High Court in the capital, Abuja, has ruled on the leadership of the party.
In July, judge Musa Liman said Mark had been chosen in accordance with the country's laws and the party's constitution - in a case brought by another former ADC member.
Abubakar said the latest case raised serious legal concerns: "Why, after that judgment, was another case filed to reopen the same dispute?"
In a statement, the ADC added that Thursday's judgement by Justice Peter Lifu was aimed at stifling the opposition momentum and "was a calculated attempt to weaken the ADC and frustrate" Abubakar's candidacy.
What happens next?
The ADC says it will challenge the ruling at the Court of Appeal.
In a statement on X, Abubakar, 79, said it showed the "panic was real" by those who felt threatened by his candidacy, external.
He said the timing of the judgment was telling as it came "barely a day after a mammoth crowd turned out in Sokoto [northern Nigeria] to welcome him" at the launch of his campaign.
"The people of Sokoto came out in their thousands because they are hungry for change and believe in our promise to make life affordable again. What we witnessed in Sokoto is only the beginning."
Political parties in Nigeria have increasingly been taking internal issues to court.
But as it stands, the electoral commission has issued its final list of candidates, external - and Abubakar is on the ticket for the ADC with former Rivers State Governor Rotimi Amaechi as his running mate.
Will the latest ruling affect the opposition?
The ADC is seen as the most powerful opposition to President Tinubu. Many influential politicians opposed to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) have already defected to the party.
The legal saga could complicate things - it may cause uncertainty for hundreds of ADC candidates as well as raise questions over who has the authority to represent them.
But Abubakar, who is running for the presidency for a seventh time, is confident the matter will be resolved and called on his supporters not to be distracted.
"Nigerians deserve relief from this crushing cost-of-living crisis. We urge our supporters to remain resolute, take our message from house to house and door to door, and stay peaceful and focused," the 79-year-old said.
Peter Obi - the other main presidential candidate, who is on the ballot for a second time - has said he is shocked by Thursday's high court ruling.
He released a statement on X with the heading, external: "Do not undermine democracy".
The 65-year-old went on to say: "My concern is that three months before a general election, it is in the public interest to have certainty.
Obi had briefly joined the ADC before leaving earlier this year to join the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) - in part because of the legal challenges within the ADC.
"The sustenance of democracy in Nigeria, in the midst of encroaching military rule in West Africa, should strengthen our resolve to protect opposition politics and not stamp out opposition parties," he said.
The NDC's candidate said that, as president, he would ensure that the existence of opposition parties would be respected.
"This is a time to strengthen our democracy by allowing the opposition to thrive."
